Lessons.Title: Solving Radical Equations
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Calculate solutions to radical equations. Create radical equations that have either zero, one, or two solutions. Explain the steps taken to solve radical equations.
Isolate the radical, impose its real domain and nonnegative output, square, solve, and substitute into the unsquared equation.

Source activity 9.1: Math Talk: Radical Equations: Solve these equations mentally: \(\sqrt[3]{x} = 1\) \(\sqrt{7} = \sqrt{x-1}\) \(\sqrt{100} = 2x\) \(\sqrt{x + 1} = \text{-}5\) Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 9.2: Getting to the Root of the Problem: Find the solution(s) to each of these equations, or explain why there is no solution. \(\sqrt{a - 5} = 5\) \(\sqrt[3]{a - 5} = 5\) \( \sqrt[3]{b} = \text{-}2\) \(\sqrt{c} + 2 = 0\) \(\sqrt[3]{3 - d} + 4 = 0\) \(\sqrt{7} = \sqrt{x-1}\) \(22z = \sqrt[3]{11}\) Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 9.3: Write Your Own Equation: Write an equation that includes a radical symbol with: Switch with a partner and solve their equations. Find all solutions to the equation \(\sqrt{x} = \sqrt[3]{x}\). Explain how you know those are all of the solutions. Whenever we have an equation with a radical symbol that contains a variable, we can solve it by isolating the radical and then raising each side of the… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Practice Problem 1: Find the solution(s) to each of these equations, or explain why there is no solution. \(\sqrt{x+5}+7 = 10\) \(\sqrt{x-2}+3=\text-2\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 2: For each equation, decide how many solutions it has and explain how you know. \(x^3 -7 = \text-20\) \(6 \boldcdot \sqrt[3]{x} = 0\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: Jada was solving the equation \(\sqrt{6-x}=\text-16\). She was about to square each side, but then she realized she could give an answer without doing any algebra. What did she realize? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: Here are the steps Tyler took to solve the equation \(\sqrt{x+3}=\text-5\). \(\begin{align} \sqrt{x+3} & =\text-5 \\ x+3 &=25 \\ x &=22 \\ \end{align} \) Check Tyler’s answer: Is the equation true if \(x=22\)? Explain or show your reasoning. What mistake did Tyler make? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: Complete the table. Use powers of 16 in the top row and radicals or rational numbers in the bottom row. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 6: Which are the solutions to the equation \(x^3=35\)? \(\text-\sqrt[3]{35}\) both \(\sqrt[3]{35}\) and \(\text-\sqrt[3]{35}\) The equation has no solutions. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Edulytics independent cool-down: Solve sqrt(x+5)=x-1. Expected reasoning or answer: x=4.
